title: How Americans view the relationship between the government and the news media
summary: Republicans and Democrats largely agree that the Trump administration and the U.S. news media have a bad relationship.

title: How Americans think about corporate and political influence on the news
summary: Roughly half of U.S. adults say news organizations are influenced a great deal by corporations and government interests.

title: Where Americans view the limits of press freedom
summary: U.S. adults hold a wide range of opinions on what's acceptable for news organizations to report and how the government should treat journalists.

title: How Americans think about censorship of news in the U.S.
summary: Substantial shares of U.S. adults think the government, news organizations and social media companies intentionally keep news from reaching the public.

title: How Americans define press freedom in their own words
summary: U.S. adults define press freedom in varying ways but many bring up the ability to report or publish information freely.

title: How much do Americans know about the First Amendment?
summary: About half of U.S. adults correctly identified that the First Amendment guarantees freedom of the press.

title: Americans Value Press Freedom but Differ on Its Limits
summary: Many people in the U.S. say some press freedom restrictions are OK when weighed against concerns about false information or national security.

title: Quiz: How much do you know about the First Amendment?
summary: How well do you know the First Amendment, including press freedom and other rights? Test your knowledge by taking our quiz.

title: The U.S. Constitution is among the hardest in the world to amend
summary: Of all 101 democratic constitutions we examined, the U.S. Constitution has the second-most onerous amendment process.

title: About 8 in 10 Americans take supplements, and many see them as important to their health
summary: About eight-in-ten U.S. adults say they are currently taking at least one supplement for their health, according to a new Pew Research Center survey.

title: The U.S. Electorate’s Changing Racial and Ethnic Makeup
summary: The share of eligible voters who are White has declined since 2006, while the Hispanic and Asian shares have nearly doubled. The share of Black eligible voters has changed little over the same period.
